parameters.comment:
EV Wallet HK — on-demand rate update normalizer.

Trigger: webhook POST /webhook/evw-rate-normalize (path set on the Webhook node). External providers (or our partner integration team) push rate-card updates here when their ToU pricing changes mid-day (the 30-min pollers are too slow for those events).

Body shape — one of:
  { provider: 'hkev', station_external_id: '...', poles: [ { external_id, hourly_rates: [...] } ] }
  { provider: 'clp'|'shell', rates: [ { station_external_id, pole_external_id, day_of_week, hour_start_local, price_per_kwh_hkd, ... } ] }

Auth: shared secret in the X-EVW-Webhook-Token header (validated by FastAPI on POST /api/v1/internal/rates/bulk-upsert). n8n simply forwards the body.

Expected runtime: <2s per call (one inbound webhook → one Code node → one HTTP POST).

Failure modes:
  * Malformed body (no poles[]/rates[]) → Code node throws, StopAndError branches on the error output.
  * Provider unknown → Code node throws.
  * FastAPI 5xx → retry 3× then StopAndError.
  * 401/403 (webhook token rejected) → no retry, StopAndError immediately.

Idempotency: hourly_rates has a unique key on (pole_id, day_of_week, hour_start_local, valid_from). Re-delivery of the same payload re-upserts the same row and is therefore a no-op on data, but does bump updated_at — that is intentional, it's how we know the provider is alive.

Single Code node that fans the payload out per-rate. Output is N items, each with { station_external_id, pole_external_id, provider_code, day_of_week, ... }. The downstream HTTP Request node runs once per item.
Per-rate call. If volume is high we can switch to batch mode by sending all rows in a single body — for now per-row keeps idempotency obvious and retries cheap.
